title: Briefing: Italy, India, Albania, Canada, France and South Africa
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Friday, October thirtieth. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means only one source has it so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.

Italy. A Milan judge orders the release of the alleged administrator of the Movimento 17 Ottobre Telegram group, held since October twenty-fourth on suspicion of incitement, saying there are no serious grounds to believe he committed the offences. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Reuters, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

India. The Cockroach Janta Party announced its support for the opposition INDIA bloc's scheduled November first rally, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter deletions during the Special Intensive Revision exercise, Deccan Chronicle and Outlook report. We grade that confirmed: independent outlets report it.

Albania. The Guardian reports that Albania's government adopted legislative measures imposing fines of up to 500,000 leks for individuals who remain in a crowd where violence, looting, or identity concealment occurs. Our grade: reported, from a single source so far.

Canada. British Columbia's Conservative Party wins a majority government in the snap election Premier David Eby called for October twenty-fourth, in which the pipeline was a campaign issue, CTV News declares. We grade that confirmed: CTV News and CBC News reported it independently.

France. The interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, in marches over the cost of living and the high-school movement; the CGT union puts both figures at nearly double the official count. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Al Jazeera, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

South Africa. Police arrest five men, aged 19 to 46, outside the Home Affairs offices on Che Guevara Road in Umbilo as persons of interest in the murder, attempted murder and assault cases linked to the unrest, Netshiunda says, IOL reports. We grade that reported: so far only IOL has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.

Albania's student protests. The Guardian reports that the leaderless protest movement began peacefully in May with rallies against a luxury hotel project in a nature reserve backed by the US president's son-in-law Jared Kushner, before morphing into student-led anti-government protests in mid-October. Our grade: reported, from a single source so far.
South Africa's asylum ruling unrest. Coming up: local government elections on November fourth.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
